spec.description:
Active Count: number of volumes that served I/O over the selected time range.

Active Consumed Capacity: total capacity currently stored across active volumes.

Inactive Count: number of volumes that served no measurable I/O over the selected time range.

Inactive Consumed Capacity: total capacity currently stored across inactive volumes.

Lists the storage pools whose subscribed capacity exceeds their usable capacity.

Capacity: total usable capacity of the pool available for data.

Subscribed: capacity committed to hosts through volumes mapped to initiators.

Subscription %: ratio of Subscribed to Capacity. Above 100% means the pool is oversubscribed, more capacity has been promised than physically exists.

Consumed Capacity %: share of the pool's usable capacity currently storing data.

Consumed Capacity % Change: change in Consumed Capacity % over the selected time range. Positive values indicate growth.

Growth Rate: rate at which consumed capacity is increasing, averaged over the selected time range.

Time Until Saturation: projected time until the pool's free capacity is fully consumed, assuming consumption keeps growing at the current rate. Pools that are flat or shrinking have no value.

Breaks the volumes into three categories based on whether each volume is mapped to a host and whether it has served any I/O over the displayed time range.

Mapped & Active - Count: number of volumes mapped to a host that have served I/O over the selected range.

Mapped & Active - Consumed Capacity: capacity currently storing data across the active volumes.

Mapped & Inactive - Count: number of volumes mapped to a host but idle over the selected range.

Mapped & Inactive - Consumed Capacity: space that is exposed to a host but not being used. This is often a sign of stale or forgotten volumes still holding data.

Unmapped - Count: number of volumes that exist but are not mapped to any host.

Unmapped - Consumed Capacity: space consumed on the array that no host can reach. Possibly a strong candidate for reclamation.

spec.title: Network Traffic - Total
spec.description:
Total network throughput across all ports on the storage system, split by direction.

Transmitted: bytes per second sent out of the storage system's ports.

Received: bytes per second arriving on the storage system's ports.

spec.title: Traffic: $network_id
spec.description:
Per-port network throughput across every port on the storage system, split by direction. 

One sub-chart is drawn per port, letting you identify which specific port is carrying the traffic shown in the Total chart above.

Transmitted: bytes per second sent out of the port.

Received: bytes per second arriving on the port.

Lists every network port discovered on the storage system. Not all columns are reported by every platform.

Name: port name as reported by the array.

Attachment Type: kind of component the port is attached to (for example, a controller, a node, or an enclosure).

Attachment ID: identifier of the component the port is attached to.

Type: kind of network interface (for example, Fibre Channel, iSCSI, or Ethernet).

Role: functional role of the port (for example, Front-end or Back-end).

Address: physical network address of the port. Typically a WWN for Fibre Channel ports or a MAC address for Ethernet ports.

Link Status: physical link state of the port (up or down).

Status: operational status of the port, classified as OK, Degraded, or Failed.

spec.title: LUNs
spec.description: Total number of NetApp LUNs discovered on the storage system.

spec.title: Total Consumed Capacity
spec.description: Sum of the capacity currently storing data across all NetApp LUNs on the storage system.

Breaks the NetApp LUNs into three categories based on whether each LUN is mapped to a host and whether it has served any I/O over the selected time range.

Mapped & Active - Count: number of LUNs mapped to a host that have served I/O over the selected range.

Mapped & Active - Consumed Capacity: capacity currently storing data across the active LUNs.

Mapped & Inactive - Count: number of LUNs mapped to a host but idle over the range.

Mapped & Inactive - Consumed Capacity: space that is exposed to a host but not being used. This often a sign of stale or forgotten volumes still holding data.

Unmapped - Count: number of LUNs that exist but are not mapped to any host.
Unmapped - Consumed Capacity: space consumed on the array that no host can reach. Possibly a strong candidate for reclamation.

spec.title: Reclaimable Consumed Capacity
spec.description:
Breaks down the total consumed LUN capacity into categories that indicate how much space could potentially be recovered.

Reclaimable Capacity (Inactive or Unmapped): consumed capacity of LUNs that are either unmapped, or mapped but idle over the selected time range.

Failed LUN Capacity: consumed capacity of LUNs that are mapped to a host but report a failed state.

Active Capacity: consumed capacity of LUNs that are mapped to a host and actively serving I/O.

spec.expr:
# Total consumed capacity of all volumes
sum(storage_usage_bytes{host_name=~"$host_name", netapp_storage_type="lun", storage_provisioning_state="used"})

Active Consumed Capacity: total capacity currently stored across active volumes.

Inactive Count: number of volumes that served no measurable I/O over the selected time range.

Name: volume name as reported by ONTAP.

Visible Capacity: configured size of the volume in ONTAP.

Available: capacity still free within the volume.

Consumed: capacity currently storing data within the volume.

Transfers: combined read and write throughput in bytes per second, averaged over the displayed time range.

Type: style of the FlexVol hosting the LUN.

Visible Capacity: configured size of the LUN as reported by ONTAP.

Available: capacity still free within the LUN.

Consumed: capacity currently storing data within the LUN.

spec.title: Ambient Temperature
spec.description: The current estimated internal temperature of the storage system.

spec.title: Heating Margin
spec.description:
The number of degrees Celsius (°C) remaining before the temperature reaches the closest warning temperature threshold of the host.

A value of 0 indicates a critical temperature.

spec.title: Read/Write Ratio
spec.description:
Share of total I/O operations that are reads versus writes, averaged over the selected time range.

Read: fraction of operations that are reads.

Write: fraction of operations that are writes.

The two values sum to 100% when there is activity; fully idle periods show nothing.

spec.expr:
(
  rate(storage_operations_total{host_name="$host_name", storage_type="storage_system", storage_io_direction="read"}[$__range]) 
/ ignoring(storage_io_direction)
  sum without(storage_io_direction) (
    rate(storage_operations_total{host_name="$host_name", storage_type="storage_system"}[$__range])
  )
) unless sum(rate(storage_operations_total{host_name="$host_name", storage_type="storage_system"}[$__range])) == 0

(
  rate(storage_operations_total{host_name="$host_name", storage_type="storage_system", storage_io_direction="write"}[$__range]) 
/ ignoring(storage_io_direction)
  sum without(storage_io_direction) (
    rate(storage_operations_total{host_name="$host_name", storage_type="storage_system"}[$__range])
  )
) unless sum(rate(storage_operations_total{host_name="$host_name", storage_type="storage_system"}[$__range])) == 0

spec.title: Thin Provisioning Commitment
spec.description:
Ratio of subscribed (promised) capacity to the system's usable capacity, expressed as a percentage.

A value above 100% means the system is thin provisioned: more capacity has been promised to hosts than physically exists.

spec.title: Time Until Saturation
spec.description: Projects how long until the storage system's free capacity is fully consumed, assuming usage keeps growing at the rate observed over the selected time range.

spec.title: Collect Started
spec.description: Time since MetricsHub started monitoring this system.

spec.title: Transfer Rate
spec.description:
Throughput handled by the storage system, broken down by direction

Read: bytes per second served to hosts.

Write: bytes per second accepted from hosts.

spec.title: Operation Rate
spec.description:
Total I/O operations per second handled by the storage system.

Read and write operations are summed together.

Capacity: total usable capacity of the pool available for data.

Available: capacity currently free in the pool.

Consumed: capacity in the pool currently storing data.

Subscribed: capacity committed to hosts through volumes mapped to initiators. Not all subscribed capacity is necessarily stored yet. The gap between Subscribed and Consumed reflects thin-provisioning commitment that hosts haven't written to.

Configured: total virtual capacity of all volumes carved from the pool, whether mapped to hosts or not. The gap between Configured and Subscribed reflects capacity that has been provisioned but not yet exposed to hosts.
Name and status of the MetricsHub connector(s) currently monitoring the storage system.

Lists every volume discovered on the storage system. The information available depends on what is exposed by the platform.

Volume: name of the volume as reported by the array.

Type: kind of volume reported by the array. Meaning varies by platform.

Mapping State: whether the volume is currently mapped to a host (Mapped or Not Mapped).

Host: name of the host the volume is mapped to, if any.

NAA ID: Network Address Authority identifier of the volume, as seen by hosts.

Visible Capacity: logical size of the volume as presented to hosts.

Available: portion of the volume's logical size not yet storing data.

Consumed: portion of the volume's logical size currently storing data. On thin volumes, this reflects physical allocation.

Consumed %: share of the volume's visible capacity currently storing data.

Operations: combined read and write operations per second, averaged over the selected time range.

Transfers: combined read and write throughput in bytes per second, averaged over the selected time range.

Status: operational state of the volume, classified as OK, Degraded, or Failed.

spec.title: System Response Time
spec.description:
Average duration of read and write operations handled by the storage system.

Read: mean time to serve a read operation.

Write: mean time to serve a write operation.

Average: mean time across all operations.

Compares the raw capacity installed in the storage system to what is actually usable for data.

Size: total raw capacity installed (sum of all physical drives).

Capacity: usable capacity presentable to storage pools.

Breakdown of the system's usable capacity between space already used by data and space still free.

Consumed: capacity currently storing data.

Available: capacity free for new allocations.

spec.title: Physical Disks
spec.description: Number of physical disks discovered on the storage system.

spec.title: Unhealthy Disks
spec.description:
Number of physical disks that need attention.

To be counted, a disk has to be either in a failed state or has less than 10% of its endurance remaining.

spec.expr:
(sum(hw_status{host_name=~"$host_name", hw_type="physical_disk", state=~"degraded|failed|missing"}) or vector(0))
+
(sum(hw_physical_disk_endurance_utilization_ratio{host_name=~"$host_name", state="remaining"} < 0.1) or vector(0))

spec.title: Size
spec.description: Sum of the raw capacity of every physical disk discovered on the storage system.

spec.title: Projected Consumed Capacity
spec.description: Linear projection of how much of the system's usable capacity will be consumed by data at the end of the period, based on the current growth trend.

spec.title: Volumes
spec.description: Total number of volumes discovered on the storage system.

spec.title: Vendor and Model
spec.description: The vendor, family and model information of the storage system

spec.title: Hosts
spec.description:
Number of distinct hosts (or host groups) to which at least one volume is mapped. 

Counts unique values of the consumer name across all mapped volumes on the storage system.

Aggregates volume capacity and I/O by the host (or host group) the volumes are mapped to. Rows with multiple hosts (e.g. "hci-esx-01,hci-esx-02") correspond to a masking view shared between hosts.

Consumer Name: name of the host, cluster, or initiator group to which the volumes are mapped.

Visible Capacity: total logical capacity of all volumes mapped to this consumer.

Consumed Capacity: total capacity currently storing data across those volumes.

Operations: combined read and write operations per second across the consumer's volumes, averaged over the selected time range.

Operations Trendline: sparkline of the operations rate
.
Transfers: combined read and write throughput in bytes per second across the consumer's volumes, averaged over the selected time range.

Transfers Trendline: sparkline of the transfer rate.
